"It's as if the market suddenly got tired of investing in the companies that fund the AI buildout (the hyperscalers) and into the companies that may benefit from AI and broader growth." Charlie Bilello, chief market strategist at Creative Planning, highlighted the apparent contradiction in current market dynamics. "So let me get this straight… Semiconductor stocks (SMH), (SOXX) are up 107% this year.
because they're spending hundreds of billions on semiconductors.
The market expects this capex cycle to continue indefinitely," he said. Bilello characterized the investing narrative succinctly: "Buy the companies selling the shovels.

And assume the spending never slows." Peter Berezin, chief economist at BCA Research, noted uneven supply chain reactions. "For companies making turbines, it's like 'Sorry, we're sold out; check back in five years.' For memory, it's 'yes, we have what you need, but we will charge you 1000% more,'" he said.
